import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlation >= 0.6)
    keep = []
    used = set()
    for i, fid in enumerate(ids):
        if fid in used:
            continue
        keep.append(i)
        # Find correlated features to mark as used
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if ids[j] in used:
                continue
            corr = np.corrcoef(x[:,i], x[:,j])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                used.add(ids[j])
    
    ids = [ids[i] for i in keep]
    x = x[:, keep]
    
    # Compute t-statistics for all features
    tstats = []
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        group0 = x[y==0, i]
        group1 = x[y==1, i]
        tstat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
        tstats.append(abs(tstat))
    
    # Select top features by t-statistic
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(tstats)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    drivers = tuple([ids[i] for i in sorted_indices if tstats[i] > 1.0])
    
    # If no strong drivers, return empty design
    if not drivers:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # For logistic regression, use all features with significant t-stats
    columns = tuple(ids)
    
    # Check for interactions among top features
    products = []
    top_indices = sorted_indices[:min(3, len(sorted_indices))]
    for i in range(len(top_indices)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_indices)):
            a, b = ids[top_indices[i]], ids[top_indices[j]]
            products.append((a, b))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, idx in enumerate(top_indices):
        loadings[ids[idx]] = tstats[idx] / max(tstats)
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
